body:
Assessment scope: M1 only, preparatory shared dependency extraction in commit b805a0b3 against 57851896. The eleven engineering subjects below cover all source, canonical/generated schema, builder and test changes. The two changed initiative record files supply author evidence and work context, not extra implementation. Current approved Proposal, exact three-model Design and clarified Delivery package were checked against inspected identities. M1 TG-01 applies; six-format retirement, schema2 discovery, recovery rejection changes and public guidance adoption remain M2–M4 work.

Spec alignment — pass. Neutral advanced schema1 transport is separated from stored-v1 representation without changing version domains. Canonical transport schema contains precisely the nine definitions reachable from the existing result shape; an independent JSON comparison found all nine byte-structure-equivalent to the old definitions and no unresolved references. The new validator copies JSON-domain, Unicode, depth, closed-field, closed-vocabulary, duplicate-identity and safe-path checks and the existing operation/status/diagnostic/snapshot-presence consistency checks. No permissive unknown-value fall-through was introduced.

Architecture and composed paths — pass. Non-inspect envelopes use the neutral owner. V2 inspected results validate their actual envelope then continue through their existing exact manifest, membership, order, content, identity, missing-record observation and revision checks. V1 and absent inspected snapshots remain on the old validator in this deliberately preparatory milestone; that retained dependency is allocated for M2 removal. Result schema1 is not confused with stored-v1. Store construction validates the same ID/safe-directory boundary using v2's own change.json path; subsequent selected-format and journal behavior is unchanged. Exact v1/v2 ID and safe-path checks were inspected; no current acceptance retirement is inferred.

Compatibility — pass. Constrained YAML parsing and root discovery are extracted as complete helpers, with existing lifecycle exports preserved and workflow-context importing their neutral owner directly. The parser retains document count, duplicate keys, aliases/anchors, custom tags, string-only keys, merge rejection, finite values and mapping-root diagnostics. Root lookup retains its .git/docs/changes ascent and fallback. No classifier, configuration output, lifecycle progression, dispatch or public command behavior is changed in M1. Existing sibling callers continue through the exported aliases.

Coverage and test quality — pass. The added test has a concrete closed-envelope obligation: valid schema1 passes; unknown status/diagnostic vocabulary, unsupported envelope version and wrong snapshot presence reject. It supplements existing public persistence/result and configuration suites rather than replacing their boundary proof. Existing test methods and fixtures are retained. The new missing-module red result is a construction-stage failure, not evidence that an old semantic defect existed. Author evidence records that distinction and the baseline fixture-copy setup correction truthfully.

Edges, errors and safety — pass. Inspected strict parser failures, result null-selector rejection, operation/status pairing, diagnostic category separation, snapshot owner dispatch, path bounds and preserved persistence entry points. New helpers perform no writes. Atomic transactions, lock ownership, conflict checks, retry, journal recovery and immutable record checks are unchanged and remain exercised by the current complete retained suites. No new security/privacy, secret logging or external-effect boundary is introduced.

Direct evidence — pass. Current m1-shared-dependencies is scoped to these exact engineering subjects. Inspected actual completed logs: complete V2 seven-module command 180/180 passed; npm test --prefix packages/rigorloop 489/489 passed, zero skipped; complete persistence/workflow-context pair 69/69 passed after extraction, versus recorded isolated baseline68 before the one added test. The fresh targeted rerun after unused-import cleanup is disclosed; that cleanup changes no executable behavior, so the broader completed proof remains applicable. The baseline initially omitted fixtures and did not execute, then was repaired before the reported baseline pass; no failed setup is relabeled a pass. Generator/model/record/whitespace checks are recorded separately as structural proof, not retirement execution. This reviewer reused those current runs and did not launch duplicate broad suites.

Generated currency and scope — pass. Canonical and bundled neutral schemas match; builder adds the new schema to its existing exact-copy/check list while retaining legacy generators for M2. No public adapter resources change in this milestone. No unrelated runtime refactor, capability deletion, historical archive rewrite or schema migration is present. Existing failed historical M4 activation audit and earlier failed workflow-context observation retain their own disclosed scope; this scoped M1 conclusion does not assert a universal baseline pass.

Checklist conclusion: requirements, tests, boundaries, failure handling, architecture, compatibility, security/privacy, generated output, scope and evidence are adequate for this exact preparatory milestone. No required correction or necessary owner decision emerged. Return to route for M1 disposition and dependent M2 within existing authorization; this reviewer has not changed milestone/activity state. M2, M3 and M4 remain. Fresh independent final whole-change Code Review after all implementation/corrections and separate successful Verify are still required. Branch readiness, PR readiness, successful retirement, CI success and final Verify are not claimed.
independence_basis: Separate delegated reviewer /root/independent_proposal_review did not author or edit any M1 engineering contribution. Independently inspected complete actual diff, new helpers/schema and relevant existing consumers, approved upstream package and current proof. Earlier independent upstream reviews are not implementation authorship. Writes only this review and its applicability.
